clues.text: This city grew in a wide river valley, near where two rivers join. Old canals drew river water out to farm fields in the dry land.
clues.narrowing: Rules out hill and coast towns; puts the player in a river valley farmed by canals.

source.quote: Phoenix was settled in 1867 as an agricultural community near the confluence of the Salt and Gila Rivers

clues.text: Night brings little relief from the heat in this city. Roads and walls soak up the sun all day, then let the heat out after dark.
clues.narrowing: Rules out places that cool at night; keeps stored heat radiating after dark.

source.quote: Pavement, sidewalks, and buildings store the Sun's heat and radiate it at night

clues.text: In 1889, the capital of the land moved to this town. It kept that job in 1912, when the land became a state.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals moved to in 1889 and kept at statehood in 1912.

source.quote: The territorial capital moved from Prescott to Phoenix in 1889, and the territorial offices were also in City Hall

clues.text: Summer heat here beats that of any other big city in the land. Its average summer highs are the hottest of all of them.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one big city has the hottest summer highs in the country.

source.quote: Average high temperatures in summer are the hottest of any major city in the United States

clues.text: The laws of Arizona are made in this city. More folk live here than in any other state capital.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the state government sits in the most populous state capital.

source.quote: Phoenix is the fifth-most populous city in the United States and the most populous state capital

reveal.blurb: Settlers farmed by the Salt and Gila rivers here in 1867, using canals first dug long before them. The town became territorial capital in 1889 and a state capital in 1912. Phoenix is the capital of Arizona.
